name: What if my garage has low ceilings?

mainEntity.name: Can a garage with low ceiling height still be converted into a legal ADU in Los Angeles County?
mainEntity.text: Can a garage with low ceiling height still be converted into a legal ADU in Los Angeles County?

acceptedAnswer.text: Ceiling height is a major feasibility issue because a garage was not originally built as living space. If the ceiling is too low, the project may feel cramped and may not satisfy required habitable-space standards without modification. Some garages can be improved by removing or reworking the ceiling assembly, lowering the floor in limited cases, or redesigning the roof structure. Others may be too constrained to convert economically. Homeowners should not wait until after drawings are complete to check height. A quick field measurement can determine whether the space is a good candidate or whether the project should shift to another ADU type. If the ceiling is borderline, good design can still help by using lighter finishes, recessed lighting, and careful mechanical placement, but there are limits. This is one of the clearest examples of why an early feasibility review matters.
acceptedAnswer.description: Low ceilings can be one of the hardest problems in garage conversions because habitable space must meet minimum height and comfort requirements. Some garages can be modified, but others need structural changes, floor adjustments, or a different project approach.
